titulo_da: Han sagde, at han ville komme

texto: To tell what someone said use **sagde at** (said that) or **fortalte at** (said that). The sentence with **at** goes in subordinate order: the subject goes before **ikke** and **altid**: **at han ikke kunne komme**.
Example: **Hun sagde, at hun var træt.** = He said he was tired.

In a narrative with the main verb in the past, this change is usually made: present → pretérito; pretérito and perfect → pluscuamperfect; **vil** → **ville**; **skal** → **skulle**; **kan** → **kunne**.

Example: **Han sagde, at han ville komme.** = He said he would come. (Direct: «Jeg vil komme».) Time also depends on when the count happens and whether it is still in place; do not change time mechanically.

filas: Hun sagde, at hun var træt.
Han sagde, at han boede i Odense.
Hun sagde, at hun havde set filmen.
Han sagde, at han ville komme.
Hun sagde, at hun skulle arbejde.
Han sagde, at han ikke kunne komme.

frases.da: Han sagde, at han var træt, og at han ikke kunne komme.
frases.es: Dijo que estaba cansado y que no podía venir.
frases.en: He said he was tired and he couldn't come.
analisis: han sagde, at han var træt

frases.en: Did he say anything about dinner?

frases.da: Ja, han sagde, at han ville komme til middag en anden dag.
frases.es: Sí, dijo que vendría a cenar otro día.
frases.en: Yeah, he said he'd come to dinner another day.

bloques.pregunta: What does «Hun sagde, at hun var træt» mean?

opciones.explicacion: «sagde» in past: «var» (was) also passes to past.

bloques.pregunta: track: I would want (in the past)

opciones.explicacion: «vil» passes to «ville» when the main verb is in the past.
It is the present; it does not change in the sentence with «at».

bloques.frase: Hun sagde, at hun ikke kunne komme.

opciones.texto: He said he didn't want to come.

bloques.audio: Han sagde, at han boede i Odense.

opciones.texto: He said he lived in Odense.
He says he lives in Odense.
He said he'll live in Odense.

bloques.pregunta: How do you change «vil» to «Jeg vil komme» when you move to «han sagde at»?

opciones.explicacion: When the main verb is in the past, «vil» → «ville».
It doesn't change: that would be the present.
That's another verb, «Come» in the present.

bloques.pregunta: How do you say «He said he'd seen the movie.» in Danish?
respuestas: han sagde, at han havde set filmen
hun sagde, at hun havde set filmen
bloques.explicacion: The past is used here because the verb was already past.

intro: Today you learn to tell what someone else said. In Danish, as in Spanish, the time of the verb changes.
